newsitem.title: USA: Quick & Reilly stock jumps amid talk of sale.
newsitem.headline: Quick & Reilly stock jumps amid talk of sale.

text.p: The stock of brokerage firm Quick & Reilly Group Inc. surged Tuesday amid a report the company has hired an investment banker to solicit a buyer for the company.

The Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday that the Palm Beach, Fla.-based Quick had retained investment banks Gleacher Natwest and Goldman Sachs to explore the sale of the company. Citing people familiar with the situation, the paper said the brokerage could fetch as much as $1.5 billion in a sale.
Quick & Reilly's stock rose $2.6875 to $32 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Quick & Reilly would not comment, saying in a statement, "As a matter of policy, we do not comment on rumours or speculation about Quick & Reilly's involvement in mergers and acquisitions.

"We feel we are strategically positioned for growth. We have the right strategy in place to continue to build upon one of the brokerage industry's most outstanding performance records. We are committed to continuing to build shareholder value, and see many opportunities to do so on our own."

Rumours had been circulating recently about further consolidation in the brokerage industry but speculation has centred on full-service firms such as Salomon Inc. and Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc., rather than the discount brokerages.
Citing unnamed sources, the Wall Street Journal reported that at least one potential acquiror had been contacted regarding a possible offer for Quick.
In another news report, First Union Corp. and Barnett Banks Inc. were identified as likely bidders.
"We're not going to be able to comment on that. It's a longstanding policy," a First Union spokesman said.
A Barnett spokeswoman said, "Our policy is that we never comment on rumours or speculation about potential aquisitions."
